publication.scope: The user requested publication of the previous batch followed by preparation of these three reports. This new batch is locally integrated and tested, not included in the previous release.

content.existing_foundations: Reused existing probability, Fourier analysis, differential geometry, functional analysis, dynamical systems and first-batch PDE pages. Knowledge prerequisites are separate from bibliography, examples and navigation.

mathematical_review.scope: Every new topic page was read by a reviewer distinct from its writer. Exact reading ranges, source corrections, local proofs, cited results and unexpanded research proofs are recorded per report. This is not a full rereading of the entire recursively reachable prerequisite corpus.

source_checks.new_test_scope: Report order, navigation, unique titles, source and prerequisite links, reachability, dependency acyclicity, exact review hashes, collision conservation, Couette transport signs and self-similar exponents. Numerical examples supplement, not replace, the written proofs.

build.theme_and_search: Existing reading theme, Chinese labels and search assets passed checks.

mathematics_rendering.new_diagram: 4620 uses the existing editable Sterling-style tikz-cd/SVG construction.

browser.final_build_retest: The first complete rebuild changed eight HTML outputs relative to an earlier preview. All 124 pages were tested again after the final rebuild; the earlier browser pass is not substituted for the final pass.

visual_review.checked: Chinese headings and paragraphs, bibliography metadata, display equations, horizontal formula scrolling and the Wigner covariance diagram. Final Deng detail screenshots were refreshed and reread after rebuilding.

scope_boundary: These reports have substantial narrative and atomic coverage, with local definitions, calculations and proofs. The per-report remaining_branches and unexpanded_deep_proofs fields identify research-level results not re-proved here. Static and graph tests do not establish semantic completeness or the correctness of every cited theorem. No claim of a completed BananaSpace terminology comparison is made.
